user.title: Connect bObsweep vacuum (local)
user.description:
This integration talks to the vacuum directly on your LAN over the Tuya local protocol — no cloud account or login is used.

**Host**: the vacuum's LAN IP address. A DHCP reservation on your router is strongly recommended so this doesn't change later.

**Device ID** and **Local Key**: these are NOT your Tuya account credentials. They must be extracted out-of-band from your Tuya/bObsweep app's local data (e.g. via a rooted phone or emulator, or the `tinytuya` wizard/scanner tool) before starting this flow.

**Protocol version**: the Tuya local protocol version your device speaks (try 3.3 first if unsure).

**Model family**: which bObsweep datapoint map to use. Pick the one your model is listed under — the datapoint ids and command values are different per family, so the wrong choice leaves entities blank and commands ignored.

error.cannot_connect: Could not connect to the vacuum at that host. Check the IP address and that the device is powered on and reachable.
error.invalid_auth: Connected, but the device ID / local key was rejected. Re-extract them from your Tuya app data and try again.
error.unknown: Unexpected error while validating the connection.

abort.already_configured: This vacuum (by device ID) is already configured.

init.title: bObsweep options
init.description:
**Approximate position from obstacle detections** — off by default, and worth understanding before turning on.

This robot has no working datapoint that reports where it is (the path-trail datapoint was tested through a full cleaning job and never returned a single point). What it does report is the obstacles its camera finds — and because it spots them directly in front of itself, a brand-new detection is roughly where the robot was standing at the time.

That is a rough indication, not localisation. It only produces a reading when the robot finds something new on the floor, which may be a handful of times in a whole clean and never at all in a tidy room, and the reading is offset by however far ahead the camera saw.

Enable it and the `current_room` sensor will start using it to guess which taught zone the robot is in. Room changes need several agreeing readings before they are confirmed, but with evidence this sparse the sensor can still name the wrong room — so do not build anything safety-relevant on it. Leave it off and `current_room` stays *unknown*, which is the honest answer.

The **Detected obstacles** sensor works either way; this setting only controls whether obstacle positions are also used to guess the room.

data_description.ai_object_position: Sparse and approximate. Off means the current-room sensor reports unknown instead of guessing.

set_mode.name: Set work mode
set_mode.description: Write a raw Tuya work-mode value to the robot's work-mode datapoint. The accepted values depend on the configured model family.

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: The Tuya work-mode enum value to send.

empty_dustbin.name: Empty dustbin
empty_dustbin.description: Trigger the auto-empty dock to empty the robot's onboard dustbin. Only the SLAM family has a self-emptying dock.

set_dp.name: Set datapoint (raw)
set_dp.description: Advanced/debug: write a raw value to an arbitrary Tuya datapoint by id.

dp.name: Datapoint id
dp.description: The Tuya datapoint id to write (as a string, e.g. "3").

value.name: Value
value.description: The value to write (string, integer, or boolean).

capture_point.name: Capture point
capture_point.description: Record the robot's current position into a scratch buffer under a label. Fails with an explanation if the robot cannot report a position.

label.name: Label
label.description: A name for this point, e.g. "kitchen NW corner".

start_zone_capture.name: Start zone capture
start_zone_capture.description: Begin recording the robot's position into a named capture session. Drive the robot around the whole room, then call Stop zone capture.

name.name: Zone name
name.description: The room name to save the captured footprint under.

stop_zone_capture.name: Stop zone capture
stop_zone_capture.description: End the running capture session, derive a room footprint from the sampled positions, and save it as a zone.

delete_zone.name: Delete zone
delete_zone.description: Delete a stored zone by name.

name.name: Zone name
name.description: The name of the zone to delete (case-insensitive).

export_zones.name: Export zones
export_zones.description: Return the whole zone document as service response data, for backup or hand-editing.

import_zones.name: Import zones
import_zones.description: Load zones from an exported document, a bare list of zones, or a JSON string of either.

data.name: Zone data
data.description: The exported zone document, a list of zones, or JSON text.

replace.name: Replace all
replace.description: Replace the entire stored zone set instead of merging into it.

zones_stale.title: bObsweep room zones no longer match the map
zones_stale.description:
The bObsweep robot's charging dock now reports a position {drift} map cells away from where it was when the room zones were saved (the limit is {threshold}). The dock does not move, so the robot's map origin has shifted — every saved zone is now measuring the wrong part of your home.

Room reporting has been suspended: the `current_room` sensor reads *unknown* rather than confidently naming the wrong room.

To fix this, re-capture your zones with the `bobsweep.start_zone_capture` / `bobsweep.stop_zone_capture` services, or re-import a set that matches the current map with `bobsweep.import_zones`. Either one clears this issue.
